relevant.instructions: The state holds one planning item (`item.title`, `item.text`) and one anchor (`anchor.statement`, `anchor.scope`) about how sanity and quality runs are recorded and shown: the atm-bd console runs pages, the sanity ledger row (elapsed per reviewer, dev identity), the value jev_client.py returns, and the dev-sanity spawn of the LLM subagent. Does `item.text` plan, change, or depend on one of these things? Judge subject overlap only, not whether the item obeys the anchor.

criteria.no: The item leaves the page out, or names only the goal (visibility, less asking), or covers only some other part of the anchor.
criteria.unclear: The item hints at a runs page but its contents cannot be told from the text.
criteria.yes: The item includes that sanity runs page with its per-run columns, in any wording or as an example row.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` contain the concrete display `anchor.statement` asks for: a console page of sanity runs, newest first, one line per run, showing who did the work and the JEV and LLM results with their elapsed times? A wish to make results easier to see is not that display.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item is a ruled-out behaviour: it follows the anchor, is silent about it, or is about something else.
criteria.unclear: The item describes runs display or timing in a way ambiguous enough that it might or might not be a ruled-out behaviour.
criteria.yes: The item states a design or step that is one of the ruled-out behaviours.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` plan something that `anchor.statement` rules out? The anchor rules out: showing sanity runs only in dev-sanity's chat reply or rendering the runs table into that reply; having no sanity runs page or no quality runs page; listing oldest runs first or using more than one line per run; a sanity line without the dev, or without pass/fail or elapsed for JEV or for LLM; computing elapsed any other way than from the Jev client's return and a timer around the LLM subagent (for example from the gap between ledger timestamps); and rows that will never feed the OTel database. The quality line's columns, paging, and OTel export arriving in the next atm release are not ruled out. Silence is not a conflict. Judge conflict only.

results.statement: dev-sanity must spawn the sanity-stack subagent for the link whenever more than one sanity task is open (or its own inline link failed), one spawn at a time in verdict order; each spawn handles exactly one next-top layer and the close procedure runs only after it returns stacked.
results.quote: we should create a sanity-stack subagent.  IF more than 1 sanity tasks are queued, sanity agent MUST use santiy-stack subagent to do the stacking and after successful stack run the close procedure.  the sanity-stack subagent should handle a single next-top layer.  multiple sanity complete sanity-stack agent spawns must be done sequentially.  This should keep things from falling apart when 10 sanity tasks land at the same time. ... dealing with the 'race condition' is the most important thing the agent does.
